#3213. Stereotaxis (STXS) Q3 2026 Earnings Call Transcript

Supply constraints and new financing shape the next phase for robotic catheter growth.

Need a quote from a Motley Fool analyst? Email [email protected]

Stereotaxis, Inc. (STXS -9.65%) reported third quarter results that focused on two structural transformations: a shift toward more accessible robotic capital systems and the expansion of its recurring revenue through a proprietary portfolio of interventional catheters. Management reported that revenue growth was driven by the initial commercial impact of the GenesisX and Synchrony systems, even as supply constraints for the MAGIC catheter created a $1.9 million order backlog. The company stated that the acquisition of Robocath has closed, adding a mechanical robotic system designed for cardiology and neurointerventional fields to its portfolio. To support these transitions, the company secured up to $24 million in convertible note financing, providing a pro-forma cash balance of $16 million and a total liquidity of $28 million. Management indicated that it expects a pathway to cash-flow profitability within the next year, supported by stabilized operating expenses of approximately $8 million per quarter.

Operator: Good afternoon. Thank you for joining us for Stereotaxis Third Quarter 2026 Earnings Conference Call. Certain statements during the conference call and question and answer period to follow may relate to future events expectations, and as such, constitute forward looking statements within the meaning of the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 2000. Such statements involve known and unknown risks, uncertainties, and other factors that may cause the actual results, performance, or achievements of the company in the future to be materially different from the statements that the company's executives may make today. These risks are described in detail in our public filings with the Securities and Exchange Commission including our latest periodic report on Form 10-K or 10-Q.

We assume no duty to update these statements at this time. All participants have been placed on a listen only mode. The floor will be open for questions and comments following the presentation. As a reminder, today's call is being recorded. It is now my pleasure to turn the floor over to your host, David Fischel, Chairman and CEO of Stereotaxis.

David Leo Fischel: Thank you, operator, and good afternoon, everyone. On our last few calls, I provided significant background on our innovation and commercial strategy. I want to keep today's prepared remarks more focused on our near term priorities key updates from the past quarter and expected upcoming milestones. it is a busy and exciting period. Our near term priority is to drive forward 2 major business model transformations. The first is shifting from capital systems that require long sales construction timelines to having a portfolio of systems that can be easily installed and are therefore significantly more accessible and scalable.

The second is developing and commercializing a portfolio of disposable interventional catheters that enhance the value of our robots and provide us with a robust recurring revenue opportunity. We are fully focused on pushing these 2 major structural transformations forward, such that they are established realities and a solid foundation upon which to build a healthy, high growth, profitable company. On the capital side, the 2 primary innovations that are beginning to have a commercial impact and advance this structural transformation are GenesisX and Synchrony. GenesisX is our newest robotic system for minimally invasive procedures. It can be installed in existing operating rooms, without the need for construction or the purchase of a specific integrated X-ray.

Synchrony is our consolidated digital cockpit for the operating room. Enhancing procedure workflow and introducing intraoperative connectivity and augmented intelligence. Our revenue growth in the third quarter benefited from the initial commercial impact of these 2 technologies. System revenue of $3 million in the quarter was up 60% compared to the third quarter of last year. We benefited from partial revenue recognition from the first GenesisX system sale in the US, the first Genesis system sold in China, and multiple Synchrony systems sold and installed in the US. Installing the first GenesisX system and demonstrating their performance and reliability in the real-world settings will be significant milestones.

We are prepared to install the first GenesisX system in the US this month, and expect to install the first GenesisX system in Europe soon afterwards. A clear requirement for the broad adoption of GenesisX by hospital customers is ensuring it can be used interoperably with various standard X-rays. We have 2 significant recent milestones supporting this broad interoperability. In August, we received FDA clearance for an upgraded version of Genesis X approved to work in a compatible fashion with any nonmodified, nonintegrated X-ray. Our systems have never had this capability or broad regulatory label, with all our previous robots being tied to a specific X-ray modified to work with us.

Then at the end of October, we were delighted to enter into a collaboration with Canon. A global leader in X-ray technology. Our collaboration supports compatibility of GenesisX with their X-ray, along with co marketing of our systems together and opportunities for other technology and commercial collaborations. The first US GenesisX system will be installed alongside Canon's X-ray and we are looking forward to this first commercial installation together. Beyond the already announced first US and European GenesisX systems, We have visibility to an additional GenesisX installation early in 2027. That will work in a compatible fashion with an X-ray system from another major manufacturer.

We have a pipeline of a couple dozen GenesisX opportunities and expect commercial activity to increase meaningfully as the first systems demonstrate their performance in real-world use. The second key capital system in our portfolio is the Synchrony digital operating room system. This past quarter was the first full quarter of commercialization following FDA approval in spring. We have multiple Synchrony systems ordered, sold, and installed in the quarter. Alongside robots, but predominantly as standalone systems installed in non robotic cath labs.

We were particularly excited by the first multilab installation of Synchrony with Abbott Northwestern Hospital in Minneapolis becoming the first hospital in the world to adopt the Synchrony system as a standardized technology across its 4 cardiology catheterization labs. We have a robust pipeline of Synchrony systems with a few dozen identified as actionable within the next year. Genesis and Synchrony GenesisX and Synchrony, are independent, though synergistic, opportunities to grow capital revenue significantly. We are just in the earliest stages of commercializing these systems, but are excited by the recent accomplishments and near term milestones. And expect more consistent and substantial capital activity in the coming months.

The development and commercialization of a portfolio of robotically steered interventional catheters is the other major transformation we are driving forward. We will have several million dollars in robotic catheter revenue this year, up from just a few hundred thousand dollars last year. And this is despite significant supply constraints and the challenge of our customers needing to transition relatively abruptly from the historic change in ecosystem they have been dependent on. Robotic capital revenue in the third quarter was up over 20% sequentially from the second quarter and up over 400% from a year ago. But underperformed our expectation. Osypka, our contract manufacturer in Germany, has not been able to meet its forecast for production of MAGICatheters.

We saw no increase in MAGIC shipments in the third quarter versus the second quarter. In Europe, we are fortunate to have 2 other robotic magnetic catheters we can offer to customers through exclusive distribution rights we established with industry partners. We have pivoted to fully focusing on these catheters in Europe, and by doing so will better serve our European customers and will preserve limited magic production from Osypka for the U.S. In The US, MAGIC remains the only available catheter for customers, and we have worked hard alongside our customers to manage the painful reality of limited supply.

We entered the fourth quarter with a backlog of approximately $1.9 million in disposable orders we could not convert to revenue due to supply constraints. While continuing to work with Osypka to improve their processes, we are also fully aware of the need to establish additional supply capacity. We reached significant regulatory milestones in that effort, in recent months and see the opportunity for the shortage to be resolved in the earlier parts of 2027. Even with no improvement in shipments from Osypka, we are confident in achieving a high watermark of recurring revenue this quarter primarily driven by the shift to our alternative catheters in Europe.

It is important to keep in mind context for our annual growth in disposable revenue. It reflects significant contribution from improved razor blade business model, counteracting significant procedural pressure from limited catheter supply, and a challenging transition away from J and J. As we continue to address these headwinds and constraints, expect the power of the attractive recurring revenue business model become much more visible and impactful. While these 2 structural transformations in capital systems and disposable revenue are our clear near term focus, we continue to advance a broad innovation pipeline that will enhance our clinical impact and commercial opportunity.

This progress is often underappreciated but is a source of significant excitement internally and among our physician customers and the industry partners. Several of the most impactful innovation efforts internally include a future generation of GenesisX that will be fully wireless, battery-operated, mobile, a more robust portfolio of electrophysiology catheters including robotic pulse field ablation, a pipeline of robotically steered wires and catheters for the cardiology and neuro fields, and AI efforts that will incorporate intelligent decision support features into Synchrony and automation to our robotic platforms. In addition to these internal efforts, most notable contribution to our innovation pipeline came with the closing of the Robocath acquisition last quarter.

We have been busy working alongside our new Robocath teammates to develop their next generation robot. The R-Star system is a mechanical robot with essentially human like fingers that can hold and manipulate 5-path catheters and interventional devices in tandem. It is being designed to work as an independent robotic system for the interventional cardiology and neurointerventional fields, but will also work synergistically with Stereotaxis' robotic technology. Clinical data from a first in human study performed with the R Star system was presented a week ago at the TCT conference. It showed superb clinical results and safety across a full range of complex coronary angioplasty procedures. Our near term work with Robocath is focused on 4 specific efforts.

Addressing remaining engineering work needed to reach formal design freeze, establishing a reliable supply chain, defining more clearly a continuous innovation pipeline for R-Star, following initial launch, and enhancing R-Star with Stereotaxis' existing advanced software architecture Synchrony Digital Cockpit, and Sync Telesurgery system. All these innovations I just shared are relatively advanced. Some will have an initial commercial impact in 2027, and all of them are in a maturing stage where they should have a commercial impact within the next 2 years. Our ability to advance so many complex technologies in parallel is a testament to the strength of our team.

It highlights our global leadership in the technological race, to make endovascular robotics an impactful reality in the large unaddressed markets of electrophysiology, interventional cardiology, and neuro interventions. Before handing the call to Kimberly, to discuss our financial results, I want to step back for a moment and make 1 general comment. I know that it may not feel like it, from the vantage view of the capital markets but this is a highly exciting period for stereotaxis. In my nearly 10 years here, I have never felt as proud of what we have accomplished and as confident about the opportunity ahead of us.

There are obviously stresses and challenges that weigh on us, but these are being addressed in a diligent fashion. It has been a long journey with some bumps on the path, but what we have brought together is remarkable. The core technology ecosystem we developed, and our in house capabilities to expand on those technologies are a very solid foundation. Our vision for what Stereotaxis can accomplish is becoming increasingly clear and tangible. We are enthusiastically advancing forward. Kimberly will now provide commentary on our financial results and then I will make a few financial comments as well before opening the call to Q&A. Kimberly?

Kimberly R. Peery: Thank you, David, and good afternoon, everyone. Revenue for the third quarter of 2026 totaled $8.9 million a 20% increase compared to $7.5 million in the prior year third quarter and a 16% increase sequentially compared to $7.7 million in the second quarter of 2026. System revenue for the third quarter was $3 million compared to $1.9 million in the prior year third quarter. System revenue in the current quarter benefited from partial revenue recognition on the shipment of the first Genesis X system sold in the United States the first Genesis system sold in China, and the first full quarter of Synchrony system sales. Recurring revenue for the third quarter was $5.9 million.

An increase of 6% compared to the prior year third quarter and a decline of 4% sequentially. Recurring revenue in the quarter benefited from a significant increase in revenue from our new portfolio of robotically navigated catheters, countered by general pressure on procedures due to supply shortages of the magic catheter and the transition away from Johnson and Johnson. Gross margin for the third quarter of 2026 was 45% of revenue. System and recurring revenue gross margin were 15%, 59%. Gross margins for both system and recurring revenue are impacted by overhead allocation over low manufacturing volume.

While we expect margins to remain at these approximate levels over the near term, we see significant opportunity for margin expansion in 2027 and 2028. Operating expenses in the quarter of $10.4 million included $1.3 million in noncash charges for stock compensation expense, mark to market adjustment for acquisition related contingent earn out consideration, and amortization of acquired intangible assets. Excluding these noncash charges, adjusted operating expenses were $9.1 million an increase from $6.6 million in the prior year third quarter due to 1-time transaction costs and higher expenses following the acquisition of Robocath. We believe it is reasonable to model future adjusted operating expenses excluding noncash and onetime item, at approximately $8 million per quarter.

Operating loss and net loss in the third quarter of 2026 were both $6.5 million consistent with the prior year. Adjusted operating loss and adjusted net loss for the quarter excluding noncash charges, were $5.1 million and $5.2 million compared with $2.5 million and $2.4 million in the previous year with the increase predominantly driven by 1-time transaction costs and higher expenses following the acquisition of Robocath. Negative cash flow for the third quarter was $6.5 million of which $2.6 million was associated with the Stereotaxis core business and $3.9 million were payments associated with the acquisition of Robocath. At September 30, Stereotaxis had cash and cash equivalents of $4 million.

Concurrent with today's financial results, we announced the convertible note financing with $12 million funded upfront and an optional additional $12 million available at Stereotaxis' discretion following certain regulatory milestones. On a pro forma basis, taking into consideration the proceeds of this financing, Stereotaxis would have $16 million in cash and cash equivalents. I will now hand the call back to David.

David Leo Fischel: Thank you, Kimberly. As Kim just mentioned, concurrent with our quarterly results, we announced the closing of a financing for up to $24 million. We appreciate the strong support we received from our long term investors. The structure of the financing is a convertible note with an initial $12 million upfront investment and then an additional $12 million optional draw. This structure reflects our belief that the financing bridges us to profitability within the next year. The conversion price of the note is at a 30% premium to our recent stock price, and interest is due at maturity in 3 years.

The incremental $12 million optional drop is contingent on a regulatory milestone we expect in the coming month, that addresses the supply constraint we have experienced with MAGIC. Upon achievement of the milestone, we would have the option but not the obligation to draw the additional $12 million in funding. With this financing, we have $16 million in pro forma cash on our balance sheet, and access to an additional $12 million for total availability of $28 million. We had significant nonrecurring expenses in the quarter related to the closing of the Robocath acquisition. The ongoing costs will be more modest. Even as we aggressively advance development of the next generation R-Star system.

Having Robocath under our belt for the past 4 months I am delighted that we made the acquisition. it is an attractive and differentiated technology, with Stereotaxis adding significant value through our expertise and synergistic capabilities, and I am confident we will turn the technology into a highly impactful and valuable asset. We expect growing recurring revenue and more consistent capital sales in the coming quarters. 2 near term milestones that support this include installing the first commercial GenesisX system, and resolving the supply constraints with Magic. We expect the coming months to be an event rich period.

With expected growth in recurring revenue and a more reliable tempo of capital sales, we see a clear pathway to profitability next year. We will now take your questions. Operator, can you please open the line to Q&A We will now begin the question and answer session.

Joshua Jennings: Hi. Good afternoon. I wanted to, David, just how are you doing? David Leo Fischel: Yeah. Sure. Happy to answer that. Thanks for the question. I think both those 2 conferences that you mentioned, both the robotic symposium at HRS in the springtime. And then just a month ago, we had the SCRN Society for Cardiac Robotic Navigation Conference. in Europe. Both of those were very well attended, far better attended than ever in the past. And we had an enthusiastic kind of physician base attending it. So, those were both very uplifting events.

I would say that there is generally among our existing user base, there is all of them are going through the process of switching from an ecosystem that they were long used to the new ecosystem with our own catheters and with different mapping systems shifting away from Johnson and Johnson. And that is a great and smooth process for some. For others, it is more challenging. But we have been working with site-by-site to get through whatever administrative hurdles work in that process. And to make sure they are comfortable with the new technology setup.

I feel that kind of we are overall working through that process in a diligent, thoughtful fashion, and I feel kind of it is always tough to change things in health care. To change things that have been working for them for many years, but I think overall, we are working through that in a good fashion. The shortage of catheters in the US does create an additional layer of stress for those sites. We are fortunate that those sites then understand our situation, understand the difficulty, and overall, we are able to work with them despite that challenge.

And I think if you look at kind of the overall space beyond our existing users, you have many physicians that are starting to look at us again given the new technologies that we received approval for over the recent months. And are intrigued by our innovations, are engaging with us more. We definitely have a pipeline that is more exciting than it is ever been in the past. There is an aspect of proving that pipeline works, making sure we can supply that pipeline, and then and then capitalizing it through actual orders and new installations.

And if you have been following us, kind of our press release and social media, we obviously had 2 new installations, new launches of robotic labs in Europe over the over the last quarter, both of them in greenfield sites, Both of those launches have gone very well so far. We see kind of a pipeline with GenesisX that we believe we will be able to capitalize much more meaningfully as we demonstrate GenesisX working in the real world. As we demonstrate compatibility with multiple different X-ray systems in these next few months. And so, overall, it feels relatively good.

I would say the 1 big macro pressure to some extent on the space, and you see it with others in the electrophysiology. Field. If you look at, let's say, you know, companies, let's say, the surgical ablation space or some others, is that the rise of PFA has definitely served as a bit of a distraction for many physicians. And so we have made significant progress even just in most recent weeks on pairing PFA with our robotic system, particularly first in Europe, but whatever we do in Europe, will come ultimately to the US. And.

But that definitely has served as a bit of a distraction in the field where even in procedures where PFA is not so relevant and in areas where the robot is not being pressured by PFA from a competitive perspective. Just from a mind share perspective, there is obviously been the 4 big players in this field, have very big microphones, and they have created a lot of other distractions in the field over this time. I think that kind of will play itself out, and I do not see that as a direct competitive threat to robotics at all. But still, that is something that is distracting.

Joshua Jennings: I appreciate that answer. And just to follow-up, I mean, I know we have touched on this in some recent discussions, but just thinking about the opportunity in pediatric electrophysiology. it is an area where PFA is not penetrating, but maybe you could just touch on how Stereotaxis is positioned there and whether demand is increasing and then how you see that opportunity evolving and maybe size it up Just have 1 last follow-up.

David Leo Fischel: Sure. Sure. So, I think maybe if I step back a little bit with some context, the cardiac ablation market is now $16 billion-plus annual medical device market. And obviously, it is still a small player, we leverage our differentiation. And where our differentiated technology provides the most clinical value for physicians and hospitals. And that is typically in the more complex procedures.

And you look at MAGIC, it is actually 1 of the things that is most unique and exciting about the catheter is it is the only catheter ablation catheter that has ever been approved for patients with congenital heart disease by FDA. And so that is obviously a very unique label and it kind of leans upon our strength in being able to treat some of these very complex anatomies where traditional catheters cannot be used or cannot be used successfully. And so that is kind of clearly an area of differentiated focus.

We have seen the vast majority of use of robotics over the last years has been in things like congenital heart disease, pediatric patients, complex ventricular tachycardias, premature ventricular contractions, these types of kind of complex procedures where we provide the most value. We also see that some physicians decide to use the robot across the full breadth of procedures. And so we have sites that use it kind of, also in simpler arrhythmias, and across the full breadth of arrhythmia types. And when I look at something like pediatrics, I think that is. it is a niche of the EP market. it is probably about 1% or so of that $16 billion market. And.

But it is a definitely underserved niche. And so pediatrics is an underserved niche. Congenital heart disease is an underserved niche. VT and PVCs are probably about 10% of the market, but they are definitely a challenging part of the EP field where we are really a particularly useful tool. And so I think kind of as you look at some of those niches, that is where you will see we continue to focus most of our innovation effort. And as we build good beachheads and demonstrate our ability to take 1%, 2%, 3% of the market.

And, obviously, just doing that would give us a revenue opportunity in the several hundreds of millions, if not, you know, billion dollar revenue opportunity. So, order of magnitude from where we are today, as we start to demonstrate our technology much more at scale in those niches, I think that you will see that our robot will naturally be used, and we will have more and more opportunities also in simple procedures down the complexity curve. So that is kind of our overall strategy as we look at the EP market.

Joshua Jennings: Excellent. And then just lastly, congratulations on the collaboration partnership with Canon Medical for Alphenix imaging platform and integration with GenesisX. But wanted to just see what the initial reaction has been and maybe talk about some of the synergies and potential cross selling opportunities and how this partnership can help as you move forward into this Genesis X commercial launch phase.

David Leo Fischel: David Fischel: Sure. So, I talked about kind of the key structural transformations, to our business model that are playing out and that we are driving forward right now. And, obviously, 1 of the major ones is that, historically, whenever a hospital or a physician wanted to adopt a robot, we needed to install it with a modified special X-ray. And transitioning from that style of capital sales, which is to something that can be installed with existing X rays that are not modified in existing cath labs that do not require construction, that is a major change to our business model, and it opens up the opportunity for, obviously, much easier adoption, much higher scale of adoption.

And we have been advancing compatibility, whether it is unilateral or bilateral compatibility, between GenesisX with the primary X rays out there in the field. We were delighted that with Canon, we are able to make this announcement, which is obviously an effort to have compatibility from both sides and to promote the system from both sides. And Canon has an X-ray that is actually the fourth largest player globally, but an X-ray that is actually particularly adopted in things like pediatrics going to your previous question, and so we are delighted with the collaboration.

We think that kind of the public aspect and the dual aspect of it does make it easier for hospitals, makes it more comfortable for hospitals to adopt our technology together. And there are definitely ways, both by allowing the co marketing and through technology things, there is ways to make the joint solution even more attractive over time. And so we are delighted to be starting this effort with them and think there is more to come in our collaboration both with Canon and in demonstrating compatibility also with other X-ray systems.

Operator: Your next question comes from the line of Daniel Stauder from Citizens Bank. Your line is live.

Daniel Stauder: Yeah. Great. Thanks for taking the questions. Just my first 1 on the catheter supply ramp. I appreciate the update here. I guess it is with Osypka not meeting their supply expectations. Where are they today in terms of per month catheters? And then that improvement that you expect in early 2027. You said 500 catheters per month watermark. And I just wanna make sure I am understanding that correctly. What exactly is going into your efforts in resolving this shortage in that time frame being early 27? Thank you.

David Leo Fischel: Yep. Thanks for the question. that is obviously a key question. That is the center point of everything related to the second big business model change in terms of kind of driving the recurring revenue opportunity. And it has been, highly disappointing, that our contract manufacturer has not been able to ramp as expected. They have grossly underperformed their own expectations for the year in the ramp, and we have essentially seen. We saw some ramp up early in the year, and then have essentially. You know, there were little kind of green shoots of potential improvement, where we thought that there was improvement, and then kind of they had supply challenges again.

This is primarily in how they increase their yields, per production and in being able to hire talented enough staff that have good yield in the production process. And for whatever reason, despite this being their business to manufacture catheters, they have had particular difficulty with the MAGIC catheter and have not been able to ramp as expected. We have essentially seen since at some point in, in the second quarter and the third quarter had the same overall volume. which is still kind of far below what would be needed to manage the procedural demand both in Europe and the US. it is also lower even with now shifting in Europe.

To alternative catheters. it is lower than what is needed just for the US. And we have talked previously about wanting to reach 500 catheters per month in production. And that would be supplying all of the procedural needs for the robot given our installed base globally. We in the prepared remarks, I talked about how while we still work with Osypka to try to improve their processes and to help them increase their yields. We also recognize that dependency carries with its risk, and it would be valuable to have redundancy in the supply chain.

And we are fortunate to have in house capabilities that are very good and that have proven themselves very well over the last couple years. And I want to talk about things somewhat vaguely. And I think that is the prudent thing for our business overall and for our relationships with other parties. But we have made. We have had regulatory milestones in that effort to set up redundant catheter supply, and I believe that with certain regulatory decisions that we believe would be reasonable to achieve in the earlier parts of next year. We would essentially have redundant supply that would fulfill the demand, especially all the demand from the US.

And that ultimately could also serve as demand for Europe. And so that is kind of the effort that has been underway. We have invested significantly in that effort over the last couple years and we think that we are getting towards the late stages of that being a reality.

Daniel Stauder: Great. I appreciate it. And just 1 follow-up. Just thinking about the backlog, I know you said there was $1.9 million that you could not convert in the third quarter. But I was curious if that is changed since then. How much have you been able to work through? How much of that is at risk as we think about your commentary on fourth quarter with recurring revenue for maybe achieving, you know, a high watermark. Just anything more you can give us on how that is developed since the end of Q3. Thank you.

David Leo Fischel: Sure. So I would say that some of that backlog is most of that backlog was dependent on magic production. The shift in Europe to. And kind of really pivoting where as our sales team was working with each individual site, to kind of have that site shift orders or not order any more MAGICatheters and instead order the 2 alternative catheters that we have exclusive distribution rights to. That helped a lot. In Europe, essentially, that is resolving all of the supply difficulties and then. And we have made that decision during the summertime, essentially. We started kind of to pivot fully into making sure MAGICatheters only come to the US to resolve the difficulties in The US.

And kind of shifting the commercial efforts in Europe. To focusing on the 2 other catheters. And I think what you will see is that you know, probably with the with the backlog that we entered this quarter, probably about half of that, if not a little bit more than half of that will be resolved in this quarter. We also will continue to receive catheters from Osypka, that will resolve some of that backlog in the US, and we will, some orders that we are able to resolve intra-quarter normally with a disposables, do not have long lead times typically for us. We build up inventory of catheters that we are able to build up inventory with.

And so, kind of that is where we have confidence given what we have done in Europe and given even just a baseline level of magic shipments from Osypka, we have confidence in meaningful growth against sequentially in disposable capital revenue and in overall recurring revenue, in the fourth quarter versus the third quarter, but it still will be pressured. it is still without an increase in MAGIC production, we still will not be able to fill all of that backlog. there is just some of that particularly in the US where we remain limited.

We are making investments in that alternative supply effort to ensure that once we have a regulatory approval, we would essentially be able to supply all of the backlog, within days of, of getting regulatory approval. And so that does require real investment. We are we are comfortable making that investment. And so that is something that we have been very focused on to make sure that, when the opportunity presents itself, we are ready to supply the customers in a full fashion.

Operator: Your final question comes from the line of Frank Takkinen from Lake Street Capital Markets. Your line is live.

Frank Takkinen: Hi, David. Hi, Kimberly. it is Wes on for Frank. Thanks for taking the question. Sounds like Synchrony placements have gone pretty well over the quarter. Pretty curious, how should we think about Synchrony's contribution through the end of the year? And can you provide us any initial thoughts through 2027?

David Leo Fischel: Sure. Thanks for the question. And so I would say that kind of we had a, you know, roughly a handful,. More than a handful of systems installed so far. And we kind of previously were talking about a million dollars a quarter. And I think in the near term, that is a reasonable expectation. But I would also say that we have a pipeline that is very kind of nice to look at. We have many, many individual hospitals. And many hospitals that are looking at multiple systems like what we discussed in the prepared remarks, at Northwestern Hospital in Minnesota, which ordered 4-- actually, 5, but had 4 installed already, kind of standardizing their cath labs on us.

We have other hospitals that are looking to do the same, and some have 3 or 4 systems, and some have 7 systems. And so there is definitely a pipeline of about 50 or so, Synchrony systems that are in our pipeline just over the next few months, less than the next year. And so that is kind of exciting. We are still in the very early stages. Right? This was just the first quarter of sales and first full quarter of sales, so we are really kind of just working through, how do we commercialize things, how do we deal through contracts, We have kind of been, becoming more efficient and effective in those processes.

Overall, I would not be surprised if we start to see quarters where we have a couple of million dollars of system sales in a quarter from Synchrony. And then as we kind of anniversary these system installations, that is when the recurring revenue of service contracts and then software as a service subscriptions starts to kick in. So, hopefully, kind of also at some point towards the end of next year, definitely in 2028, you will start to see also a more meaningful recurring revenue opportunities from the system.

Frank Takkinen: Awesome. that is very helpful. Thank you.

Operator: That concludes our question and answer session. I will now turn it back over to David Leo Fischel for closing remarks.

David Leo Fischel: Okay. Thank you very much for all the questions and for your continued support. We will work hard to finish this year strong, and wish you all a healthy and successful end of the year. Thank you.

#3212. New Apple TV 4K remote’s best feature requires a newer iPhone model

A new Apple TV 4K releases this Friday (pre-order here), with an upgraded Siri Remote. But the new remote’s best feature might not work on your iPhone.

If you’re interested in the new Apple TV 4K launching this week, or perhaps you just want to buy the upgraded Siri Remote separately (available here), there’s a key limitation you should know.

Precision Finding on the new Siri Remote requires an iPhone 17 or newer.

The most common problem with the current Siri Remote is that it’s easy to lose. And once you lose it, Apple doesn’t offer many options for finding it. But that’s changing with the 4th gen Siri Remote.

You can use the new Siri Remote with any previous Apple TV 4K or Apple TV HD model. And if you do, you’ll benefit from the remote’s new built-in speaker that can be triggered from the Find My app.

Joining the new speaker, the other main change with this latest Siri Remote is Precision Finding. If you’ve ever used the Find My app to track down a lost AirTag, you’ll probably be familiar with the feature.

Precision Finding lets you get step-by-step, guided directions that take you directly to the lost Siri Remote. It’s a huge upgrade from the old tool for finding the remote—which mostly just told you that it’s in your house somewhere.

But Precision Finding relies on the Bluetooth 6 support found in iPhone 17 and 17 Pro models (not iPhone 17e), iPhone Air, iPhone Duo, and iPhone 18 Pro models.

So if you don’t have one of those iPhones, you’ll still benefit from the built-in speaker that lets you play a sound to find the lost remote, but Precision Finding won’t be available.

You can buy the new Siri Remote for $59 on Amazon.

Will this limitation impact your Siri Remote purchase decision? Let us know in the comments.

#3211. Ohio State and Microsoft sign a five-year AI and cloud hospital deal

The deal expands AI note-taking for doctors and aims to shift up to 80% of the university's computing to Azure.

Ohio State and Microsoft signed a five-year AI and cloud partnership.

Ohio State University and Microsoft signed a five-year partnership to move up to 80% of the university’s storage and computing to Azure, expand AI note-drafting at its Wexner Medical Center and build “smart hospital” systems. No financial terms were disclosed.

Ohio State University and Microsoft have signed a five-year deal to bring more AI and cloud computing into the university’s Wexner Medical Center, Microsoft said on Tuesday. Neither side disclosed financial terms.

The biggest shift is in infrastructure. Ohio State aims to move 70% to 80% of its storage and computing to Microsoft’s Azure cloud, including pathology and medical imaging. It will also keep a backup of its electronic health records on Azure, so staff can still reach them if its own systems fail.

Doctors already use Microsoft’s Dragon Copilot to draft notes from patient visits, which they then check and sign off. Such AI scribes can still make serious errors, as NHS records showed this year.

Other parts are earlier. Two Ohio State buildings run a “smart hospital” system that links building and clinical equipment to save energy. A shared data platform for forecasting things like surgery demand and staffing is still at the design stage, and an AI tool for cancer case reviews is only being explored.

“Artificial intelligence represents one of the most significant opportunities to transform and improve how hospitals care for patients,” said John J. Warner, the medical centre’s chief executive.

Big tech firms are racing to sell AI to health systems. NHS England is rolling out Microsoft’s Copilot to 505,000 staff, and Google Cloud launched Gemini for healthcare on the same day as the Ohio State deal. Amazon’s AWS also unveiled a $100M health programme.

#3210. Apple announces Swift Student Challenge 2027 with new twist

Apple has announced details for 2027’s Swift Student Challenge, and there’s a new twist this year: students can submit an app for any Apple platform.

Apple is proud to support the next generation of developers, creators, and entrepreneurs with the Swift Student Challenge. The Challenge gives students from around the world the opportunity to showcase their creativity and app development skills.

Submissions are open February 8–28, 2027. And new this year, students can submit an app for any Apple platform. Sign up now to get notifications about student activities.

February 8-28 is still a few months away, but Apple wants to give participants plenty of time to plan ahead and start working on their entry sooner rather than later.

And in an exciting change, students can build an app for any platform this year, including tvOS, visionOS, watchOS, and more.

This opens fresh opportunities for creativity, especially on Apple’s less saturated app platforms.

Apple will once again recognize winners across two tiers: “winners” and “distinguished winners.” The latter will be invited to join Apple in Cupertino “for an incredible experience.” All winners will receive a one-year Apple Developer program membership and a special gift.

Will you participate in the Swift Student Challenge this coming year? Let us know in the comments.

#3209. IEEE Program Schools Preuniversity Educators On Tech Topics

The TryEngineering workshops help teachers deliver engaging STEM lessons

An educator constructs a microchip model during the IEEE Making a Microchip lesson plan demonstration.

Now in their third year, the IEEE TryEngineering educator sessions continue to empower preuniversity teachers with specialized professional development programs on engineering topics and classroom-tested lessons.

This year’s sessions, held across the United States, have focused on educating teachers about artificial intelligence and semiconductor technology. One session was held in Egypt.

In all, 54 educators learned about the engineering design process this year. They received an overview of TryEngineering resources including the Making of a Microchip and Train Your Tree lesson plans.

Workshops are scheduled this year in Greece and Guatemala.

The TryEngineering program is administered by IEEE Educational Activities.

These teachers and guest speakers attended the two-day session held at the Florida Semiconductor Institute and SkyWater Technology chip manufacturing facility.IEEE Educational Activities

Central to the educator session program’s success is its university network. Host campuses welcome teachers into their facilities, where faculty provide background information about some of the technologies being taught, as well as possible engineering career paths and job opportunities for students.

This year’s sessions involved the educators in hands-on projects. Facilitators at each location were selected based on their experience in engineering education, and they worked with the TryEngineering staff on their presentations.

Sixteen teachers from nine schools participated in the session, held in Cairo. It was facilitated by Marwa Soudi, an IEEE member, and Senior Member Stamatis Dragoumanos. Both are past chairs of the IEEE preuniversity coordinating committee. GEMS provided outstanding STEM facilities for teachers, Saudi and Dragoumanos said. Participants received an overview of the Working With Wind Energy and Tall Tower Challenge lesson plans.

Another educator session is scheduled for later this year.

Educators from across the state gathered at the university’s Florida Semiconductor Institute, headquartered in Gainesville, and FSI’s NeoCity high-tech manufacturing campus near Orlando. The session was hosted by Roseanne Perez, an FSI workforce development program specialist, and Sophia Watson, FSI’s assistant director of workforce development. The two-day experience featured an inside look at microelectronics through a guided tour of a SkyWater Technology chip manufacturing facility.

Engineering instructor Mary Acken facilitated hands-on lesson demonstrations for the 15 attending teachers.

Reflecting on the workshop’s impact, one participant said the SkyWater tour was excellent, the instructors were great, and the teachers enjoyed learning from like-minded educators.

Michael Kozicki, an IEEE member, and Stefan Myhajlenko from the university’s engineering school welcomed 11 Arizona teachers to the Tempe campus.

The session was facilitated by Janet Hartkopf, an Arizona school leader and a former TryEngineering educator session participant. Hartkopf highlighted collaborative learning, the need for diverse perspectives in engineering education, and career paths.

The teachers received instruction on how to implement the hands-on lessons in their classrooms, and they toured the university’s NanoFab facility to observe microelectronics research.

“This training was amazing!” said a participant who leads an elementary after-school STEM club. “I loved the hands-on lessons and e-books, which I will definitely be using with my students. I am excited to explore all the resources on the TryEngineering website. The experts from ASU were great.”

Sixteen STEM educators attended this session, held at the university’s International Institute for Biosensing in Minneapolis. Its director, Patricia Khashayar, an IEEE member, introduced participants to the capabilities of the university’s Supercomputing Institute and Nano Center.

Under the guidance of Claire Dietz, an education and outreach coordinator, and Pam Schumacher, an instructor at St. Paul College, the teachers completed classroom-ready lessons including a photonics experiment using the Nano Center’s equipment. Schumacher attended last year’s TryEngineering educator session.

Nano Center Director Sarah Swisher, an IEEE senior member, provided an overview of semiconductor operations and highlighted growing job opportunities for the state’s young people.

The experience inspired all 16 teachers to plan student field trips to the Nano Center during the upcoming academic year, they said.

“Great class!” one participant said. “I’m excited to bring some of the TryEngineering materials back to our school.”

This year’s sessions built on the momentum from last year when, with financial support from Onsemi’s Giving Now program, nearly 80 teachers attended sessions across five U.S. states and Mexico.

Driven by that success and the demand for more, the IEEE Educational Activities Board continued its support. Upcoming global sessions are expected to expand the program’s international footprint.

“I appreciated the time to collaborate with peers on how to implement hands-on lessons,” one participating teacher this year said. Some participants said they planned follow-up visits with the experts and campus tours.

You can learn more about the sessions by emailing TryEngineering.

Debra Gulick is director of IEEE student and academic educational programs.

#3208. Nvidia says it cut off Megaspeed in 2025, but Bloomberg found later imports

Bloomberg also found that Nvidia’s count of Megaspeed chips sold through partners ran 50,000 short. Nvidia’s lawyer had called a top Commerce official about Alice Huang’s detention in Singapore.

Nvidia says it banned all sales and shipments to Megaspeed in June 2025, and that the ban is still in place, a company spokesman told The Wall Street Journal. Since then, Commerce has allowed Nvidia to send it parts and replacement components, the spokesman said.

Malaysian trade records show that Megaspeed imported at least 17,544 of Nvidia’s GB300 chips, worth about $787m, in November 2025, Mackenzie Hawkins reported for Bloomberg. Nvidia gave US officials a count of chips sold to Megaspeed through hardware partners. It was 50,000 units short, Bloomberg found. Megaspeed is still an official Nvidia Cloud Partner. TNW has not independently verified the reports.

Megaspeed is the Singapore company at the centre of the Jensen Huang affair. Nvidia’s board opened an independent investigation after Huang admitted an affair with Alice Huang, a Megaspeed executive. US officials believe she is a Chinese intelligence asset. China has denied the espionage claims.

In mid-November 2025, Nvidia told Bloomberg that its inventory checks found everything where it should be. It also said it had asked the US government whether it needed to cut off Megaspeed, and was told no.

In December 2025, Nvidia told Bloomberg it had checked more warehouses that held the missing hardware. It did not say how many chips it found. Two of the eight data centre operators Nvidia told Washington it had visited said they had no Megaspeed hardware. Nvidia declined to comment on that to Bloomberg. Megaspeed’s largest landlord has since dropped it as a tenant.

About three months ago, Nvidia general counsel Tim Teter told a White House official that Alice Huang was “not as important” in Megaspeed as she made out, according to a person familiar with the call. He said that, because of the bad publicity around her, Nvidia had stopped doing business with Megaspeed.

In late summer 2025, Teter called Jeffrey Kessler, the Commerce under secretary in charge of chip export curbs. He asked whether Kessler’s Bureau of Industry and Security had a role in Singapore’s detention of Alice Huang. It did not, people familiar with the matter told Bloomberg. An Nvidia spokesperson said Teter did not know about the affair at the time.

It is unclear whether Teter made any specific requests of Kessler, according to Bloomberg. In the following weeks, bureau staff were told to route all requests of Nvidia through Kessler or get his approval. The people called that highly unusual, and unique to Nvidia. Staff were also told not to name Megaspeed or Speedmatrix, its Malaysian subsidiary, in external communications.

In late 2025, the Justice Department, which was working on the Megaspeed smuggling case with the bureau, asked it to pause. The bureau has made no progress since, despite having enough evidence to move forward, Bloomberg reported.

“BIS conducts all enforcement strictly by the book,” a bureau spokesman said.

“We work to resolve any allegations of ‘diversion’ promptly, to help government and our partners halt any would-be smugglers while serving the critical market of lawful customers that help America win worldwide,” an Nvidia spokesperson told Bloomberg.

In December 2023, Jensen Huang and a small group of colleagues met Alice Huang at an Italian restaurant in Singapore, according to The New York Times. She had just restructured Megaspeed. Four days after its ownership change, Nvidia named it a cloud partner, the Times reported on Tuesday.

Megaspeed went on to secure more than $4bn of Nvidia chips. In late 2024, the Commerce Department sent an official to inspect one of its data centres, where some Nvidia equipment was still packed in boxes. That year, Taiwan began monitoring Alice Huang’s trips to the island at the suggestion of the US government, a person familiar with the matter told the Times.

In 2025, Singapore barred her from leaving and questioned her in a probe into false import declarations. The investigations against her were closed for lack of evidence, the person said, but Singapore is still investigating Megaspeed. She later flew to Shanghai.

Megaspeed has categorically denied the chip diversion allegations. It told Bloomberg that Singapore’s probe ended this year with no adverse action against it. Its outreach to the US government went unanswered, it said. Nvidia and Megaspeed declined to comment to the Times. Alice Huang did not respond to the Times, and Bloomberg has been unable to reach her.

Senators Jim Banks, a Republican, and Elizabeth Warren, a Democrat, urged Commerce to suspend or reconsider Nvidia’s China export licences, Bloomberg reported. Their bill would temporarily bar Nvidia from selling Chinese customers any chip more advanced than the H200. Lawmakers are negotiating to add it to the annual defence bill, which typically passes in December.

“I think we’re going to work hard to make sure that those provisions make it into the final version of the National Defense Authorization Act,” House Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries said.

Senator Richard Blumenthal wants a Senate investigation, Semafor reported. In the House, three committee chairs have asked Huang to attend a closed briefing on 18 November.

#3207. Suja Life (SUJA) Q3 2026 Earnings Call Transcript

Softer store traffic and competitor price cuts are eroding Suja's promotional returns.

Need a quote from a Motley Fool analyst? Email [email protected]

Suja Life, Inc. (SUJA -4.32%) reported increased net sales and adjusted EBITDA during the third quarter, driven by volume gains in core beverage lines and expanded retail distribution. Management noted that while the company gained market share, it faced intensifying pressure in the conventional grocery channel and reduced consumer traffic. In response, the company lowered its full-year outlook to reflect current macroeconomic conditions and shifted marketing investment toward retail trade promotions to maintain competitiveness.

Operator: Good day, and thank you for standing by. Welcome to the Suja Life Third Quarter 26 Earnings Conference Call. At this time, all participants are in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. To ask a question during the session, you will need to press *11 on your telephone. You will then hear an automated message advising your hand is raised. Please be advised that today's conference is being recorded. I would now like to hand the conference over to your first speaker today, Mike Mougias, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Michael K. Mougias: Good afternoon. And welcome to Suja Life's third quarter 26 earnings call. Joining me today are Maria D. Stipp, Chief Executive Officer and Jeff Pedersen, Chief Financial Officer. Our earnings press release was published this afternoon and can be found on our Investor Relations website. Today's call is being webcast there as well. And a replay will be made available shortly after the call. Before we begin, a reminder that today's discussion will include forward looking statements. These statements reflect our current expectations and are covered by the safe harbor provisions of the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 2000. They are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially.

For more on those risks, please see today's press release and our most recent SEC filing. We assume no obligation to update these statements. We will also refer to certain non GAAP financial measures. You will find reconciliations to most comparable GAAP measures in today's press release and our SEC filings. We are unable to reconcile forward looking non GAAP measures without unreasonable effort. With that, I will turn the call over to Maria.

Maria D. Stipp: Thank you, Mike, and good afternoon, everyone. The third quarter showed what this business can do in an environment where consumers remain under pressure. Net sales grew 3% to $776.4 million ahead of the outlook we gave you in August. That includes approximately $2 million of shipments that moved from the fourth quarter into the third. Adjusted EBITDA was $10.5 million, a $9.6 million increase versus last year. 3 things stand out to me this quarter. First, consumers are choosing our brands. Suja gained share again this quarter, and our newer lines, like our refreshers, are leading the way. Second, we are winning where shoppers are going with strong growth in club and convenience.

And third, we are managing the business for profitability. We expect adjusted EBITDA to grow roughly 70% this year, with margin expanding about 7 points to nearly 20%, while investing deliberately behind our brands. That discipline is especially important given the continued pressure in grocery. Which is shaping our near term expectations. I will walk through each of these and how we are adapting our plans in response. Jeff will then take you through the numbers and our updated financial outlook. Let me start with share. In the third quarter, our share of the natural healthy beverage rose approximately 30 basis points to just over 9% according to Nielsen. Year to date, we are up more than a full point.

And in the quarter, among the category's 5 largest manufacturers, Suja was the only 1 to gain share. Those gains came amid increased promotional activity across the category and pressure on household budgets. In grocery, the percentage of natural health beverage dollars sold on promotion in the quarter increased more than 6 percentage points versus a year ago. Despite that increase, the added promotion did not translate into overall category growth. We chose carefully where to put our promotional dollars. We stepped up support behind our shots and refreshers, but we did not chase the deepest discounts in grocery where they were not paying back.

And our share gains show that consumers are still choosing our brands even with more promotion in the market. Second, shoppers continue to seek better for you products. They are buying them in different places, and we are following them. In the third quarter, our Nielsen measured sales in club grew nearly 20%. In convenience, they grew more than 40% from a small base. And in mass, they grew about 6% with more room ahead. In August, I told you we would expand our programs in club and mass. Club is our clearest win so far, driven by incremental programming on Suja organic green juices and wellness shots.

We also said we would work arm in arm with our retail partners. And we did. Through top to top sessions with several of our largest customers. Those conversations have helped secure meaningful new distribution with more reset meetings still to come. And we keep investing in our brands. Store traffic is softer. Retailers are cutting prices more deeply and promotions are delivering lower returns. As a result, we no longer expect the fourth quarter step up we planned for. We are resetting expectations and looking to concentrate slice where it is working. That brings me to the third point. How we are managing the business. Stepping back, this has been a year of real change for Suja. We became a public company Our category tightened. And we have streamlined how we operate. I think about Suja's history in 3 chapters. The first was proving we could build these brands. The second was proving that we could make them laugh. This next chapter is about scaling with intention and that means making choices. We brought our marketing, sales, and innovation teams together into 1 commercial organization.

So we can plan further ahead move faster with our retail partners, And we are directing investment into channels and platforms, and programs with the clearest returns. Owning our production gives us more control over our costs and our supply, and that is what creates room to make choices. While expanding profitability this year. Our priorities ahead are clear. First, building velocities across our portfolio. Including in our core greens juices, single serve shots, and vibe.

Leaker Aaron Perris has discovered evidence of a new Mac app in the works at Apple called Harbor, which makes it easy to run local AI models across one or more Macs.

The Mac has been getting a lot more popular this year, both because of budget-friendly options like MacBook Neo but also as a tool for running AI models locally on Mac Studio, Mac mini, and more.

It seems Apple plans to lean harder into the latter use case, as leaker Aaron Perris has discovered a new Mac app called Harbor that’s been designed to turn your Mac into a private AI inference server.

Here’s Perris’s post on X with the details:

Apple is working on a new app called HarborHarbor turns your Mac into a private AI inference server. Run open-weight models locally on Apple silicon—your data never leaves your hardware, and nothing reaches the cloud. Connect multiple Mac computers over Thunderbolt 5 to pool… pic.twitter.com/UYJBQeX4Nf

As the post notes, here’s what the app does:

Harbor turns your Mac into a private AI inference server. Run open-weight models locally on Apple silicon—your data never leaves your hardware, and nothing reaches the cloud. Connect multiple Mac computers over Thunderbolt 5 to pool unified memory, enabling large models and higher concurrency that a single computer can handle alone.

Harbor is currently in a private preview under Apple’s Claris brand, but it seems likely that we’ll see it launch to the public in the weeks and months ahead.

Are you interested in using Harbor on your Mac? Let us know in the comments.

Soundbars are expensive. That's just the fact of the matter. You can easily drop a grand on the best soundbar system, and I've even tested $3,000+ models. Unfortunately, cheap soundbars can sound flat, narrow, or tinny, and I've only ever recommended a few sub-$400 models.

However, Samsung has changed the game with this deal. The Samsung Q900F is currently just $697 at Best Buy, down from $,1497 — a huge saving of $800. The Q900F is a 2025 model, but its sound is still excellent. It has a 7.1.2 channel setup, which means there are seven speakers in the central soundbar, a separate subwoofer, and two up-firing speakers for genuine Dolby Atmos immersion. This soundbar is also compatible with the lesser-spotted DTS: X, another surround sound technology found on some DVDs and Blu-rays.

At 53% off, I presume Best Buy is trying to shift leftover Samsung stock to make room for 2026's new releases (the QS90H and the Q990H, both of which I've tested and adored), so I don't see this sticking around for long. I'd grab it before it's too late.

The Samsung Q900F is a 2025 pre-flagship model. Samsung's "Q" line refers to its premium devices and includes the flagship Q990F and the pre-flagship Q900F (this model). The Q900F has a wireless subwoofer and built-in up-firing speakers for a 7.1.2 channel configuration. In short: genuine Dolby Atmos for room-filling, movie-theater sound.

As a soundbar + subwoofer combination, the Samsung Q900F requires a decent amount of space in your living room. It's 49 inches long, so I'd recommend a TV at least 55 inches or bigger — otherwise the soundbar will dwarf your TV, and it'll look strange.

The subwoofer itself will either need to go behind or next to your sofa — you can move it around to find the optimal placement. I have my Denon subwoofer next to the sofa, but it sometimes loses connection, forcing me to shuffle it around. I've never experienced a subwoofer disconnecting like that on a Samsung soundbar, but it's still worth noting.

The Q900F has 4K pass-through at 120Hz, which makes it ideal for gamers if your TV only has one HDMI 2.1 port. This means you can plug your console into the soundbar for 4K playback with no juddering or stuttering. Other flagships, like the JBL Bar 1300X MK2, still lack this.

Now onto the most important thing: sound quality. How does the Q900F actually sound? While I haven't personally tested it, I've tested 10 Samsung soundbars, namely the 2026 flagship Q990H, Q600F, Q600H, QS750F, QS90H... the list goes on. And what do they all have in common?

They sound excellent. Samsung soundbars all sound incredible. Dialogue is clear, especially thanks to the dialogue mode (which this model has), and bass is always confident and controlled thanks to the industry-leading subwoofer. Some features, like SpaceFit Sound Pro on pre-2026 models, are restricted to post-2021 Samsung TVs; again, not a dealbreaker but worth noting.

#3204. Web Summit cancels Day 2 in Lisbon as Storm Charles hits Portugal

Portugal’s government advised Web Summit that Wednesday should not go ahead, citing flooding, transport disruption and high winds. The organisers aim to reopen on Thursday for the final day.

Web Summit’s main stage in Lisbon in November 2025

Web Summit has called off Wednesday’s programme in Lisbon because of Storm Charles. Portugal’s government advised the organisers that Day 2 should not take place. Web Summit told attendees by email on Tuesday evening that it aims to hold Day 3, on Thursday 12 November, as planned.

The government cited the risk of tidal flooding and severe disruption to public transport. It also pointed to the effect of high winds on outdoor structures, Web Summit said. The advice followed talks with the civil protection authority, ANEPC, and the Public Security Police (PSP).

“The safety and security of our attendees, staff and contractors is always our absolute priority,” the Web Summit team wrote.

Web Summit said it will keep working with the authorities and emergency services. It will contact those affected directly.

Earlier on Tuesday, Lisbon mayor Carlos Moedas said “everything indicates” the event could not run on Wednesday. Stephen Conneely reported his comments for The Irish Times. Moedas said more than 60,000 people were at the venue in Parque das Nações.

The government has declared a state of alert across mainland Portugal for Wednesday, The Portugal News reported. Schools and non-essential public services will close. Lisbon is shutting its tunnels, parks, gardens and cultural venues from midnight. The weather service IPMA forecast gusts of up to 120km/h.

Web Summit runs from 9 to 12 November. Last month, it released its tech industry survey. In it, 60% of people in tech said AI had increased their workload.

#3203. iOS 27.2 adds new features in six iPhone apps, details here

iOS 27.2 recently launched with new features for iPhone users, including improvements across six Apple apps. Here’s what’s new.

One of my favorite additions to Messages this year, Suggested Actions, debuts in iOS 27.2.

Suggested Actions appear underneath messages in a conversation when relevant. They can suggest creating a calendar event or reminder, adding to a note, and more based on the context of the message.

The feature was originally part of the iOS 27 beta this summer, but didn’t make the public build. Now it’s back in iOS 27.2, new and improved. There’s also an option to fine-tune which types of suggestions you’ll see.

Read more: iOS 27.2 adds new Messages feature that’s already a favorite

Every major streaming service has its own profiles feature, letting users on the same account keep their viewing history and recommendations separate. Apple TV has long offered such a feature in tvOS, but now with iOS 27.2 and iPadOS 27.2 it’s coming to iPhone and iPad too.

When you launch the TV app in iOS 27.2, you’ll be greeted by a new profile selection screen. You can easily disable it if you don’t want to see if again. But if you ever share your iPhone with kids, the new profiles feature should come in handy.

Read more: iOS 27.2 gives Apple TV a new profiles feature on iPhone

Dual Capture is one of FaceTime’s best new features in years. Added in iOS 27, on compatible iPhones it lets you keep your front and rear cameras both active at the same time while on a FaceTime call.

iOS 27.2 brings a key upgrade to Dual Capture: it’s now available for Group FaceTime calls.

To use the feature, just hit the flip camera button like usual, and by default on iPhone 17 and newer you’ll stream both camera feeds simultaneously.

Read more: iOS 27.2 makes FaceTime’s best new feature even better

Timed with its new Home products push, Apple adds a pair of new Home app features in iOS 27.2 for compatible smart locks.

‘Lock After Closing’ is a new automation setting that lets you choose how long after a door is closed that it should lock automatically. Previously you could only set a duration based on the time since a door was unlocked, not closed.

‘Door Left Open’ tackles a related, but distinct problem: a door being left open too long. With compatible locks, you can configure the Home app to automatically notify you if a door has been left open for a certain period of time.

Read more: iOS 27.2 has three new changes just added this week

Apple Podcasts keeps getting better, with AI-powered automatic chapters and transcripts some of my favorite features. And in iOS 27.2, Apple has a welcome change to the Up Next queue on the Home tab.

Up Next is now split into two separate queues: New Episodes and Continue Playing.

New Episodes contains only the latest episodes from shows you follow, while Continue Playing is a hub for all the episodes you’ve previously started but haven’t yet finished.

Apple’s Games app introduces some small updates in iOS 27.2 as well.

The Home tab now shows you recently downloaded games that you haven’t yet played. Previously, you would only see games with some play activity. And Apple says achievement progress and leaderboard scores have been updated in the Home tab to be easier to track. Finally, the Friends tab “provides context on friend suggestions and shows recent games played on friends’ player pages” per Apple.

Which new iOS 27.2 features are you most excited about? Let us know in the comments.
